Algebra I · Lesson 7.2

Graphing Linear Equations

Solve this lesson →All lessons

7.1 gave every ordered pair a place on the plane. From 5.1, an equation in two variables has one solution pair for every value of xx chosen, so its solutions can never be listed in full. Every one of those pairs is a point. Marking all of them at once replaces the endless list with one picture.

Problem
The graph of 3x+4y=293x+4y=29 is the set of points whose coordinates make that equation true. One of (7,2)(7,2) and (9,1)(9,1) is on the graph and the other is not. Substitute both, and enter the value the left side takes at the point that is not on the graph.
Show a hint
  • Substituting a point puts its first coordinate in for xx and its second for yy, then evaluates 3x+4y3x+4y. Do that for both points and compare each result with 2929.
  • Start with (7,2)(7,2). If 3(7)+4(2)3(7)+4(2) comes out to 2929, that point is on the graph, and the value you want is whatever 3x+4y3x+4y gives at (9,1)(9,1).
Show the full solution
Substituting (9,1)(9,1) into the left side gives 3(9)+4(1)=27+4=313(9)+4(1)=27+4=31​. The other point does satisfy the equation, since 3(7)+4(2)=21+8=293(7)+4(2)=21+8=29, so (7,2)(7,2) is on the graph and (9,1)(9,1), where the left side comes out to 3131 instead of 2929, is not.
Problem
The notation (x,8)(x,8) means a point whose second coordinate is 88 and whose first coordinate is not yet known. That point is on the graph of 5x−3y=115x−3y=11. Enter its xx-coordinate.
Show a hint
  • The number given is the second coordinate, so it is the value of yy. Substitute it and the equation has only xx left in it.
  • The equation becomes 5x−24=115x−24=11.
Show the full solution
Substituting y=8y=8 gives 5x−3(8)=115x−3(8)=11, which is 5x−24=115x−24=11. Then 5x=355x=35 and x=7x=7​. A point is on the graph exactly when its coordinates satisfy the equation, so the known coordinate goes in for its own letter and the missing one is left to solve for.
Key idea
The graph of an equation is the set of its solution points. Every solution pair (x,y)(x,y) is one point, and the graph of the equation is the collection of exactly those points and no others. A point is on the graph when substituting its two coordinates makes the equation true, and off the graph otherwise, which is 5.1's check with the pair read as a point. The test is arithmetic and not appearance. A point with fractional coordinates is on the graph whenever its substitution is true, and a point drawn close by is off the graph whenever its substitution is false.
Problem
Build a table for 3x+2y=303x+2y=30 at x=0, 2, 4, 6, 8x=0, 2, 4, 6, 8, solving for yy in each row. The five pairs all lie on one straight line, and exactly one of them has its two coordinates equal. Enter the value those two coordinates share.
Show a hint
  • Each row takes one value of xx and solves 3x+2y=303x+2y=30 for yy, so the row for x=2x=2 reads 6+2y=306+2y=30.
  • A row with equal coordinates has yy equal to its own xx, so replacing yy with xx in 3x+2y=303x+2y=30 turns it into an equation in xx alone.
Show the full solution
The rows give (0,15)(0,15), (2,12)(2,12), (4,9)(4,9), (6,6)(6,6) and (8,3)(8,3), and the pair with equal coordinates is (6,6)(6,6), so the shared value is 66​. All five pairs satisfy the equation, so all five are points of the same line, and any two of them are enough to draw it.
Problem
Exactly one of these four points is not on the graph of 4x−3y=184x−3y=18. (34,−5)(3,−2)(9,7)(12,10)(43​,−5)(3,−2)(9,7)(12,10) Enter the xx-coordinate of the point that is not.
Show a hint
  • Test all four the same way, including the one with a fractional coordinate. A fraction is a perfectly good coordinate, and all that matters is whether 4x−3y4x−3y comes out to 1818.
  • Watch the signs. At (34,−5)(43​,−5) the term −3y−3y becomes +15+15, and at (3,−2)(3,−2) it becomes +6+6.
Show the full solution
The four left sides are 3+15=183+15=18, 12+6=1812+6=18, 36−21=1536−21=15 and 48−30=1848−30=18. Only (9,7)(9,7) gives something other than 1818, and its xx-coordinate is 99​. Whether a point is on the graph depends only on what the substitution gives, not on how tidy the coordinates look, so here the fractional point is on the line and a whole-number point is not.
Key idea
The graph of ax+by=cax+by=c is a straight line. Whenever aa and bb are not both zero, the points that satisfy ax+by=cax+by=c all lie in one straight line, and every point of that line satisfies the equation. An equation of this form is a linear equation in two variables, named for that line. Through two distinct points there is exactly one straight line, so two solution pairs are enough to draw the whole graph, however many solutions the equation has in total.

Two points are enough to draw the line, so a third pair is spare, and a spare point is a check. Any two points lie in a straight line, even two computed wrongly, so an arithmetic slip is invisible with only two points. Three points in one line is a condition that can fail, so a third point off the line is proof that one of the three is wrong.

Problem
The point (4,2)(4,2) is on the graph of 7x−ky=67x−ky=6, where kk is a constant. Only one value of kk makes that true. Enter kk.
Show a hint
  • Testing a point is the same substitution whether the unknown is a coordinate or a coefficient. Putting both coordinates in leaves an equation whose only unknown is kk.
  • With x=4x=4 and y=2y=2 the equation reads 28−2k=628−2k=6. Note the minus sign in front of the kk term.
Show the full solution
Substituting gives 7(4)−k(2)=67(4)−k(2)=6, so 28−2k=628−2k=6, then 2k=222k=22 and k=11k=11​. Check, 7(4)−11(2)=28−22=67(4)−11(2)=28−22=6. The usual slip is reading −k(2)−k(2) as +2k+2k, which gives 28+2k=628+2k=6 and k=−11k=−11.
Problem
A student computes three pairs for 2x+5y=342x+5y=34 and gets (2,6)(2,6), (7,4)(7,4) and (12,3)(12,3). Plotted, the three points do not fall in a straight line, so one pair is wrong. Keep the xx-value of the pair that fails, and enter the yy-value that belongs with it.
Show a hint
  • Two of the three pairs satisfy the equation and one does not, so run the test on all three before deciding which one to fix.
  • The three left sides come out 3434, 3434 and 3939. Take the xx-value of the pair that misses and solve 2x+5y=342x+5y=34 for yy again.
Show the full solution
The three left sides are 4+30=344+30=34, 14+20=3414+20=34 and 24+15=3924+15=39, so (12,3)(12,3) is the wrong pair. At x=12x=12, 5y=34−24=105y=34−24=10 and y=2y=2​. The corrected point sits one unit below the plotted one, which is why the three looked nearly straight rather than obviously wrong. A third point is worth computing for exactly that reason.
Key idea
Plot from a table, then check with a third point. Choose a value of xx, substitute it into the equation, and solve for yy. Each row of the table is one solution pair and so one point, and two rows are enough to draw the line. The point from a third row is on that same line when all three pairs are right and off it when one of them is wrong, so a third row is worth computing before the line is drawn rather than after. Choosing values of xx for which yy is a whole number keeps every point easy to plot.

Any value of xx is allowed in the table, and two choices take less work than the rest. Where a graph crosses an axis, one coordinate is already known, so only the other is left to compute. The next two problems find those crossings, and a later pair shows that a graph need not cross both axes at all.

Problem
The graph of 3x+8y=243x+8y=24 is a straight line, and it meets the xx-axis at exactly one point. Enter the xx-coordinate of that point.
Show a hint
  • Every point of the xx-axis has y=0y=0, which 7.1 established. That is the value to substitute here.
  • With y=0y=0 the term 8y8y is 00, so the equation becomes 3x=243x=24.
Show the full solution
A point of the xx-axis has y=0y=0, so 3x+8(0)=243x+8(0)=24, which is 3x=243x=24, and x=8x=8​. Setting x=0x=0 instead gives 8y=248y=24 and y=3y=3, the crossing on the yy-axis rather than the xx-axis.
Fun fact
William Playfair published the first line graphs of economic data in 1786, in his Commercial and Political Atlas. He put time along the bottom and money up the side, so a trend could be seen rather than read from a table.
Problem
The graph of 3x−4y=483x−4y=48 is a straight line that crosses the yy-axis once. Enter the yy-coordinate of the crossing point.
Show a hint
  • Every point on the yy-axis has x=0x=0, so substitute that value and solve for yy.
  • The equation becomes −4y=48−4y=48, and the coefficient of yy is negative, so divide both sides by −4−4 and keep the sign.
Show the full solution
A point on the yy-axis has x=0x=0, so 3(0)−4y=483(0)−4y=48, which is −4y=48−4y=48, and y=−12y=−12​. Dropping the minus gives 1212 and puts the crossing above the origin instead of below it, and setting y=0y=0 by mistake gives 1616, which is the xx-axis crossing.
Key idea
The intercepts. The xx-intercept is where a graph meets the xx-axis, and every point of that axis has y=0y=0, so substituting y=0y=0 gives it. The yy-intercept is where the graph meets the yy-axis, and every point there has x=0x=0, so substituting x=0x=0 gives it. The row (0,15)(0,15) in the table for 3x+2y=303x+2y=30 has x=0x=0, so it was that graph's yy-intercept all along. Each substitution leaves a one-letter equation, so the intercepts are the two cheapest points to plot. The variable set to zero is never the one the intercept is named after.

Every equation so far has had both letters in it. In ax+by=cax+by=c only one of aa and bb has to be nonzero, so the other may be zero. With a=0a=0 what remains is by=cby=c, and dividing by bb leaves y=ky=k. With b=0b=0 what remains is x=kx=k. Each still has a graph, and the next two problems settle which points are on it.

Problem
In the coordinate plane, the graph of 2y+9=−52y+9=−5 is made of exactly the points (x,y)(x,y) that satisfy it. One of those points has first coordinate 4040. Enter that point's second coordinate.
Show a hint
  • The equation contains no xx, so the first coordinate can be anything at all. The only condition is on the second coordinate.
  • Solve 2y+9=−52y+9=−5 for yy the same way you would solve any one-variable equation. The 4040 is not needed for that work.
Show the full solution
From 2y+9=−52y+9=−5, 2y=−142y=−14 and y=−7y=−7​. Because the equation contains no xx, every point on this graph has second coordinate −7−7, whatever the first coordinate is. That is why the 4040 is not needed.
Problem
The graph of 3x=−183x=−18 is a straight line. Enter the number of points that line has in common with the yy-axis.
Show a hint
  • Solve for xx first, then describe the graph. No yy appears, so every point of the graph shares one xx-coordinate.
  • From 7.1, a point is on the yy-axis exactly when its xx-coordinate is 00. Compare that with the xx-coordinate every point of this graph has.
Show the full solution
Solving gives x=−6x=−6, so every point of the graph has first coordinate −6−6. A point of the yy-axis has first coordinate 00, and −6≠0−6=0, so the number of shared points is 00​. Reading x=−6x=−6 as a horizontal line gives the answer 11 instead, since a horizontal line does meet the yy-axis once.
Key idea
y=ky=k is a horizontal line and x=kx=k is a vertical line. A point satisfies y=ky=k exactly when its second coordinate is kk, with no condition on its first, so the graph is every point at height kk, which is a horizontal line. A point satisfies x=kx=k exactly when its first coordinate is kk, with none on its second, so the graph is the vertical line through (k,0)(k,0). The letter in the equation is the fixed coordinate, not the direction of the line. So x=kx=k has no yy-intercept unless k=0k=0, since every point of the yy-axis has first coordinate 00.

The last two problems use every piece at once. An equation is not always written in the form ax+by=cax+by=c, and terms in the same letter may appear on both sides, so collecting them onto one side comes first. A coefficient can also be unknown, and then one stated fact about the graph is enough to determine it.

Problem
The graph of 9y−4x=30+5y9y−4x=30+5y is a straight line. Enter the xx-coordinate of the point where it meets the xx-axis.
Show a hint
  • The yy terms sit on both sides. Collect them on one side first, and the equation takes the form ax+by=cax+by=c.
  • Collecting gives 4y−4x=304y−4x=30. Every point of the xx-axis has y=0y=0, so put that value in and solve for xx.
Show the full solution
Subtracting 5y5y from both sides gives 4y−4x=304y−4x=30. A point of the xx-axis has y=0y=0, so −4x=30−4x=30 and x=−152x=−215​​. Setting x=0x=0 instead gives 4y=304y=30 and y=152y=215​, which is where the line meets the yy-axis, not the xx-axis.
Problem
The graph of 6x+by=216x+by=21 has no point in common with the yy-axis, where bb is a constant. Enter the xx-coordinate of the point on that graph whose yy-coordinate is −11−11.
Show a hint
  • Substituting y=−11y=−11 straight away leaves two unknowns, so use the stated fact first. A point sits on the yy-axis exactly when its xx-coordinate is 00, so put x=0x=0 into the equation.
  • If b≠0b=0, then x=0x=0 gives by=21by=21 and a point on the yy-axis exists. The graph has no such point, so only one value of bb is possible, and the equation is left with no yy term.
Show the full solution
If b≠0b=0, setting x=0x=0 gives by=21by=21 and a point on the yy-axis. The graph has no such point, so b=0b=0 and the equation is 6x=216x=21. Every point of that graph has x=216x=621​, so the one with y=−11y=−11 has x=72x=27​​. The form ax+by=cax+by=c allows b=0b=0 as long as aa is not zero too, and here a=6a=6. With b=0b=0 the equation contains no yy, so the −11−11 is not needed.

Every graph in this lesson came from the same two steps, find two solution points and draw the line through them. Those steps settle where the line is and say nothing about how steep it is. Lesson 7.3, Slope, attaches a number to the steepness, computed from any two points of the line.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Substitute the point (6,3)(6,3) into the left side of 2x+3y=192x+3y=19, and enter the resulting value of 2x+3y2x+3y.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 2(6)+3(3)=12+9=212(6)+3(3)=12+9=21​. The left side comes out 2121 while the right side is 1919, so (6,3)(6,3) does not satisfy the equation and does not lie on the graph.
Practice
The point (4,y)(4,y) is on the graph of x+y=17x+y=17. Enter yy.
Show the solution
The point has x=4x=4, so 4+y=174+y=17 and y=13y=13​. A point is on the graph exactly when its two coordinates make the equation true, so putting in the coordinate that is given leaves one equation in one unknown.
Practice
The point (x,3)(x,3) is on the graph of 5x−2y=645x−2y=64. Enter the value of xx.
Show the solution
The point has y=3y=3, so 5x−2(3)=645x−2(3)=64, which is 5x−6=645x−6=64. Then 5x=705x=70 and x=14x=14​. Check, 5(14)−2(3)=70−6=645(14)−2(3)=70−6=64. Putting the 33 in for xx instead gives 15−2y=6415−2y=64, a different point on the same line.
Practice
The graph of 9x+2y=−89x+2y=−8 contains a point whose xx-coordinate is −2−2. Enter that point's yy-coordinate.
Show the solution
Substituting x=−2x=−2 gives 9(−2)+2y=−89(−2)+2y=−8, so −18+2y=−8−18+2y=−8, then 2y=102y=10 and y=5y=5​. Dropping the negative gives 18+2y=−818+2y=−8 and y=−13y=−13, the common wrong answer.
Practice
Three of (5,13)(5,13), (8,7)(8,7), (10,4)(10,4), (1,21)(1,21) are on the graph of 2x+y=232x+y=23 and one is not. Enter the xx-coordinate of the one that is not.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 10+13=2310+13=23, 16+7=2316+7=23, 20+4=2420+4=24 and 2+21=232+21=23. The third value is not 2323, so the point off the graph is (10,4)(10,4) and the answer is 1010​. A point is on the graph exactly when its coordinates satisfy the equation, so one failed check is enough to rule a point out.
Practice
Enter the xx-coordinate of the point where the graph of 5x+2y=605x+2y=60 meets the xx-axis.
Show the solution
Every point on the xx-axis has y=0y=0, so 5x+2(0)=605x+2(0)=60, which is 5x=605x=60, and x=12x=12​. Reversing the substitution and setting x=0x=0 gives 2y=602y=60 and y=30y=30, which is the yy-coordinate of the point where the graph meets the yy-axis.
Practice
Enter the yy-coordinate of the point where the graph of 7x−3y=427x−3y=42 meets the yy-axis.
Show the solution
Every point on the yy-axis has x=0x=0, so 7(0)−3y=427(0)−3y=42, which is −3y=42−3y=42, and y=−14y=−14​. Setting y=0y=0 instead gives 7x=427x=42 and the number 66, which is where the graph meets the xx-axis, not the yy-axis.
Practice
A point on the graph of 5y+31=65y+31=6 has first coordinate −90−90. Enter its second coordinate.
Show the solution
From 5y+31=65y+31=6, 5y=−255y=−25 and y=−5y=−5​. The equation contains no xx, so every point of this graph has second coordinate −5−5 whatever its first coordinate is, which makes the −90−90 irrelevant.
Practice
In the coordinate plane, the graph of 4x+29=54x+29=5 contains a point whose second coordinate is 4141. Enter that point's first coordinate.
Show the solution
From 4x+29=54x+29=5, subtracting 2929 gives 4x=−244x=−24, so x=−6x=−6​. The equation has no yy in it, so every point of the graph has first coordinate −6−6 whatever its second coordinate is, and the graph is the vertical line x=−6x=−6. The 4141 is not needed.
Practice
The point (2,5)(2,5) is on the graph of kx−4y=10kx−4y=10, where kk is a constant. Enter kk.
Show the solution
Substituting gives k(2)−4(5)=10k(2)−4(5)=10, so 2k−20=102k−20=10, then 2k=302k=30 and k=15k=15​. Checking it back, 15(2)−4(5)=30−20=1015(2)−4(5)=30−20=10, so (2,5)(2,5) does satisfy the equation with that value of kk.
Practice
Enter the yy-coordinate, exactly, of the point where the graph of 8x+5y=188x+5y=18 meets the yy-axis.
Show the solution
A point of the yy-axis has x=0x=0, so 8(0)+5y=188(0)+5y=18, which is 5y=185y=18, and y=185y=518​​. The crossing point is not required to have a whole-number coordinate, so keep the fraction in lowest terms rather than rounding it.
Practice
The graph of 9x=20−2y9x=20−2y crosses the xx-axis at exactly one point. Enter the xx-coordinate of that point as an exact fraction.
Show the solution
Every point on the xx-axis has y=0y=0, so the equation becomes 9x=20−2(0)=209x=20−2(0)=20, and dividing by 99 gives x=209x=920​​. Since 2020 is not a multiple of 99, the exact coordinate is that fraction, and a rounded decimal does not satisfy the equation.
Practice
A student lists (5,9)(5,9), (10,6)(10,6) and (15,4)(15,4) as points on the graph of 3x+5y=603x+5y=60. Plotted, the three do not fall in a straight line, so one pair is wrong. Keeping that pair's xx-value, enter the correct yy-value.
Show the solution
The three left sides are 15+45=6015+45=60, 30+30=6030+30=60 and 45+20=6545+20=65, so (15,4)(15,4) is the wrong pair. At x=15x=15, 5y=60−45=155y=60−45=15 and y=3y=3​. Two points always fall in one straight line, wrong ones included, so a bad pair only shows up once a third point is plotted.
Practice
Enter the number of distinct points where the graph of 4x−7y=04x−7y=0 meets an axis.
Show the solution
Both crossings are the same point, the origin, so the answer is 11​. Setting y=0y=0 gives 4x=04x=0 and so x=0x=0, and setting x=0x=0 gives −7y=0−7y=0 and so y=0y=0, which makes both crossings (0,0)(0,0). Counting one crossing per axis gives 22 and counts the origin twice.
Practice
Enter the xx-coordinate of the point where the graph of 3(x−y)=x+383(x−y)=x+38 meets the xx-axis.
Show the solution
A point on the xx-axis has y=0y=0, so 3(x−0)=x+383(x−0)=x+38, which is 3x=x+383x=x+38. Subtracting xx from both sides gives 2x=382x=38, so x=19x=19​. Setting x=0x=0 instead finds where the graph meets the yy-axis, a different point. Check, 3(19−0)=573(19−0)=57 and 19+38=5719+38=57.
Practice
The graph of px+8y=20px+8y=20 has no point in common with the xx-axis, where pp is a constant. Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that graph whose xx-coordinate is −25−25.
Show the solution
A point on the xx-axis has y=0y=0, and the equation then reads px=20px=20. If p≠0p=0 this gives the point (20p,0)(p20​,0) on the xx-axis, so p=0p=0 and the equation is 8y=208y=20. Every point of the graph has y=208y=820​, so the point with x=−25x=−25 has y=52y=25​​. With p=0p=0 the graph is the horizontal line y=52y=25​, so the xx-coordinate does not matter here.
Practice
The graph of 8y−15x=1208y−15x=120 meets the xx-axis at AA and the yy-axis at BB. Enter the distance between AA and BB.
Show the solution
Setting y=0y=0 gives −15x=120−15x=120, so x=−8x=−8 and A=(−8,0)A=(−8,0). Setting x=0x=0 gives 8y=1208y=120, so y=15y=15 and B=(0,15)B=(0,15). Then the distance is (−8−0)2+(0−15)2=64+225=289=17(−8−0)2+(0−15)2​=64+225​=289​=17​. Each crossing sits on an axis, so the horizontal gap is 88 and the vertical gap is 1515, and 82+152=17282+152=172 is why the distance comes out whole.

Reading is a start. In the course you solve each problem yourself, with instant feedback, layered hints, and Milo right beside you when you get stuck.
